description: FOUND s455d by the boxed-aggregates design probes (scratch al.pl): perl v=1x, PCL v=1 on `my %h=(a=>1); for (values %h) { $_ .= "x" }`. Probed at 90da9e8 -- pre-existing, independent of the raw-element design (elements ARE boxed today; the values list builder copies values instead of passing the slot boxes). FIX: the foreach list builder for values %h passes slot boxes (E11 in the design doc; the copy positions like my @v = values %h stay copies -- perl only aliases the foreach/alias positions). BAR: probe set both positions vs perl + guard rows + the E11 battery row; sweep (cl/ change). Sibling: #818 (slice-in-foreach). Fix naturally lands with (or before) design phase 2.  [CLOSED s457ai, commit 9c0cf75: the fix is at the LIST-BUILDER layer -- p-values / p-aslice / p-hslice / p-kv-aslice / p-kv-hslice hand out the container's own slots via %p-alias-aelem / %p-alias-helem (p-aref-argbox / p-gethash-argbox with a fallback for containers that cannot hold a slot box). The right layer was proved by probing TWELVE copy positions: a plain @a in list context has ALWAYS handed out its slot boxes and every copy consumer already unboxes, so the builders were put in that same shape rather than a second one. The sweep then caught the other half: @a[0,1] = @a[1,0] needs perl's read-the-whole-RHS-first rule, which PCL had inside %p-flatten-list and the slice-assign arms never ran -- extracted as %p-assign-snapshot. Guard: Pl/t/elem-alias-01.t (E1-E12 vs real perl).]
subject: for (values %h) { $_ .= ... } does NOT write through to the hash -- perl aliases values() in foreach, PCL copies (SILENT WRONG, pre-existing on fully-boxed main)
